lead.headline: Oil Tops $110 After Attacks in Saudi Arabia
lead.deck: The US tells some diplomats and their families to leave the kingdom.
body: Oil is a fuel that ships carry all around the world. Its price is quoted per barrel. On Thursday, Brent crude, a main world price, rose to about $110 a barrel. It had ended Wednesday at $108.82.

The price rose after attacks in Saudi Arabia, the world's big oil seller. The Houthis, a group in Yemen, hit targets in the kingdom on Wednesday. At a civilian airport in Dammam, one person was killed and eight were wounded. A drone attack near Shaybah, a Saudi oilfield, killed two people. Saudi officials said work at the oilfield was not affected. Earlier this month, the country's East-West pipeline, which carries oil to Red Sea ports, was reportedly halted after a Houthi strike hit a pumping station.

The attacks led the United States to tell some diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. Ships are under attack too. Kpler, a firm that tracks ships, counted at least 18 attacks on shipping in two weeks.

lead.why: Saudi Arabia sells oil to the whole world. When its supply is at risk, the cost of fuel and transport can rise far away.

world.headline: Putin Agrees in Principle to Restart Three-Way Talks
world.deck: Russia, Ukraine and the US could meet again after 10 November.
body: Russia's war in Ukraine is more than four years old. On Wednesday, US envoy Steve Witkoff met Russia's President Putin in St Petersburg for about three hours. Afterwards, Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov said Putin agreed, in principle, to restart three-way talks with the US and Ukraine after 10 November.

The talks would focus on building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the war ends. Earlier rounds, held in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, made little progress beyond swaps of prisoners. Ukraine's President Zelensky said only a meeting of leaders can break the deadlock, and that freezing the conflict is the minimum he needs from Russia.

Russia also freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired US teacher jailed for fighting in Ukraine, after Trump asked Putin to release him. Witkoff called it a goodwill gesture. The fighting has not paused, though. Overnight attacks on Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, killed three people and injured 12.

us.headline: Early Voting Surges Before the Midterms
us.deck: More than 13 million Americans have already voted.
body: On 3 November, Americans vote in the midterm elections. They are held halfway through a president's term, and they decide who controls Congress, the group that makes the country's laws.

Many people vote early, by mail or in person. The Associated Press, a news agency, counted early votes two weeks before election day. More than 13 million had been cast. At the same point in 2022, the last midterms, the number was 9 million.
Texas showed a big jump, with nearly 1 million early ballots against about 550,000 in 2022. Some of the rise comes from states that now offer more early voting.
us.why: Midterm elections decide who makes the nation's laws. Early votes show how many people are taking part.
also: Kansas: early votes more than doubled, to over 55,000 from 27,000 in 2022.
Ohio: early ballots are up 30%, or 156,000 more than in 2022.

india.headline: Rupee and Shares Slip as Oil Passes $110
india.deck: The central bank also says cuts in interest rates are off the table.
body: India buys much of its oil from other countries and pays in US dollars. So when oil gets dearer, Indian markets feel it. On Thursday the Sensex, a main index of share prices, fell 460.30 points to 73,249.39. The Nifty, another main index, fell for a third day in a row.
The rupee also slipped. It fell about 30 paise, to 94.81 against the US dollar. Analysts expect it to trade between 94.45 and 95.25. A weaker rupee makes imports, such as oil, cost more rupees.

The Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank, has raised its main interest rate, the repo rate, by 0.25 points to 5.50%. Its rate-setting committee voted unanimously. Minutes released on Wednesday said cuts are off the table for now, and the next move can only be a rise or a pause.
india.why: Dearer oil and a weaker rupee can push up prices at home, which is why the central bank is watching closely.

sports.body: India beat New Zealand by 4 wickets in Christchurch on Thursday, with two balls to spare. New Zealand made 225/4, and Sanju Samson hit 67 off 33 balls as India chased 226. Naman Dhir finished it with an unbeaten 42 off 15 balls and was Player of the Match.
